title: GoThru 3d Floor Map UI Design Project Report

issues.display_title: Issue #185: Update editor toolbar layout structure
issues.main_description_html:
brainstorming.md - Update Toolbar Editor Layout

branch: product-docs
file: docs\superpowers\specs\2026-07-06-editor-layout-structure-brainstorming.md
Sources: User brief, current editor topbar, current editor 2D/3D workspace, current floating toolbar behavior
Audience: Product, UI/UX, QA, and Claude UI UX Pro Max

RESULT

branch: UI-UX-Update-editor-toolbar-layout

1. Shared Understanding

Goal

Make editor mode easier to understand by separating 2D drawing tools from shared viewer controls, while keeping the current editor behavior, visual style, and compact workspace feel.

Product Intent

The editor should feel like a professional indoor mapping workspace. Users should always understand which tools affect the 2D floor plan, which controls affect the 3D viewer, and which controls apply to both. The change is mostly about layout clarity, grouping, and discoverability, not a new editor concept.

Main User Problem

The current toolbar mixes file actions, drawing tools, visibility settings, panel controls, and camera controls in one long row. This makes the workspace feel busy and can make users unsure whether a control affects the 2D panel, the 3D panel, or the whole editor.

Desired Outcome

Users should be able to answer three questions at a glance:

  • Where do I go for file-level actions?
  • Which tools do I use to draw or edit the 2D floor plan?
  • Which controls do I use to view, inspect, and adjust the 2D/3D workspace?

2. Current Layout Observations

The current editor already has useful building blocks:

  • A compact top navbar with MapThru branding, a File dropdown, save state, theme toggle, Share, Preview, and Save.
  • A 2D plan panel and a 3D view panel that can appear together or separately.
  • A floating bottom toolbar with drawing tools, undo/redo, zoom, camera, object visibility, image visibility, and panel toggles.
  • Existing visual styling with small icon buttons, rounded controls, soft borders, editor color tokens, and floating tool surfaces.
  • An Add Level flow that already owns floor and floor plan upload behavior.
  • Export-related behavior that can be grouped into one Export area instead of multiple visible toolbar buttons.

The layout does not need a full redesign. It needs stronger organization and clearer tool ownership.

3. Product Intent

Editor mode should feel calm, direct, and work-focused. The user is building a Digital Twin from a Floor Plan, so the interface should support precise work without making the control surface feel crowded.

The improved layout should:

  • Keep the existing editor identity.
  • Make 2D editing tools feel attached to the 2D plan panel.
  • Make 3D and shared viewer controls feel separate from drawing tools.
  • Keep repeated actions quick to reach.
  • Reduce disabled or duplicate controls.
  • Avoid changing the user's mental model of saving, previewing, drawing, and switching panels.

4. In Scope

  • File dropdown content and labels.
  • Bottom toolbar organization.
  • Separation between 2D-only drawing tools and shared viewer controls.
  • Placement of the Shapes dropdown inside the 2D toolbar.
  • Object visibility grouping.
  • Floor plan image visibility and opacity behavior.
  • Panel display mode naming and placement.
  • Guidance for keeping the current editor visual style.
  • Non-technical interaction guidance for UI UX Pro Max.
  • Acceptance criteria and QA scenarios for layout clarity.

5. Out of Scope

  • Rebuilding the editor engine.
  • Changing drawing behavior.
  • Defining shape creation behavior beyond toolbar placement and menu grouping.
  • Changing how walls, curves, windows, areas, points, or safety annotations are stored.
  • Changing save, autosave, preview, share, or project persistence behavior.
  • Changing Add Level behavior beyond recognizing it as the home for floor plan loading.
  • Creating a new visual design system.
  • Adding new third-party dependencies.
  • Creating backend endpoints.
  • Implementing the layout in code as part of this brainstorming document.

6. Recommended Layout Direction

Recommended Approach: Keep the Editor Shell, Split Tool Ownership

Keep the current editor shell and visual language, but reorganize actions into three clear zones:

  1. File and project actions in the top navbar File dropdown.
  2. 2D drawing tools near or inside the 2D plan workspace.
  3. Shared viewer controls in a separate compact control group for navigation, visibility, image overlay, and panel mode.

This approach is recommended because it improves clarity without changing the product too much. Users keep the same editor surface, but the controls become easier to scan and understand.

Alternatives Considered

Alternative A: Keep one long toolbar

This preserves the current structure, but it keeps mixing drawing, viewing, file, and panel actions. It does not solve the main confusion.

Alternative B: Create a full left-side professional tool dock

This could work for a larger editor redesign, but it is too large for this task. It may also change the style and behavior more than needed.

Alternative C: Move every control into top menus

This would make the canvas cleaner, but drawing tools would become slower to reach. Editor mode needs direct tool access.

7. File Dropdown Changes

Purpose

The File dropdown should contain clear project-level navigation and help actions. It should not show disabled placeholders or actions that have moved elsewhere.

Recommended Items

Menu item Destination / behavior User meaning
Dashboard Redirects to /dashboard Leave editor and return to the project workspace.
New File Redirects to /start Start a new project or new file flow.
Help Redirects to /help Open help content for the editor.

Remove From File Dropdown

  • Disabled New File placeholder, if it does not navigate.
  • Disabled Export placeholder, if export is handled by a real Export control.
  • About, unless there is a clear product requirement for it.
  • Add Floor, unless Product wants File to remain the entry point for level management.

Navigation Notes

  • Dashboard should keep the existing unsaved-change protection.
  • New File should also protect unsaved changes before leaving the editor.
  • Help may open in the same app route or a separate help surface, but the user should not lose work unexpectedly.

Suggested Copy

  • File
  • Dashboard
  • New File
  • Help
  • Unsaved changes
  • Leave without saving
  • Cancel

8. Toolbar Cleanup

Purpose

The visible editor toolbar should stop carrying file import/export actions that belong elsewhere. This keeps the main toolbar focused on active editing and viewing.

Remove From Visible Toolbar

  • Load Floorplan.
  • Save Editable TXT.
  • Export GeoJSON.

Where These Actions Belong

Current action New home Reason
Load Floorplan Add Level Loading a floor plan is part of adding or managing a level.
Save Editable TXT Export It is an output action, not a drawing tool.
Export GeoJSON Export It is an output action, not a drawing tool.

Export Group

Export should become the clear home for downloadable outputs. It can include:

  • Editable TXT.
  • GeoJSON.
  • Future export formats, if needed.

The Export group can live in the topbar or as a compact button near shared viewer controls, but it should not be mixed into the drawing tool strip.

9. Tool Grouping Strategy

Group A: 2D Drawing Tools

These tools belong to the 2D floor plan editing workflow:

  • Wall.
  • Curve.
  • Window.
  • Area.
  • Shapes.
  • Point.
  • Safety Annotation.
  • Undo.
  • Redo.

The 2D drawing tools should visually belong to the 2D panel. They should feel like tools for shaping Map Geometry and adding indoor map annotations.

Shapes Dropdown

Shapes should appear as one grouped dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools, not as three separate top-level toolbar buttons.

Recommended dropdown items:

  • Rectangle.
  • Circle.
  • Polygon.

Place Shapes near Area, Point, and Safety because it belongs to the same 2D floor plan editing surface. Shapes should remain a layout-level grouping in this document; the detailed creation behavior stays in 2026-07-06-editor-shapes-tools-brainstorming.md.

Recommended 2D tool order:

  1. Wall.
  2. Curve.
  3. Window.
  4. Area.
  5. Shapes.
  6. Point.
  7. Safety.
  8. Undo.
  9. Redo.

Group B: Shared Viewer Controls

These controls support viewing, inspecting, and managing the workspace:

  • Zoom In.
  • Zoom Out.
  • Fit Plan.
  • Reset 3D Camera.
  • Object visibility.
  • Snap to Grid.
  • Floor Plan Image visibility.
  • Floor Plan Image opacity.
  • Panel display mode.

These controls are not drawing tools. They should be grouped separately so users do not confuse viewing controls with content creation tools.

Group C: Context Selection Tools

Selection-specific actions can remain contextual:

  • Door/window size.
  • Door swing.
  • Room height.
  • Area type.
  • Wall thickness.
  • Delete selected.
  • Deselect.

These should appear only when relevant and should not crowd the default toolbar.

10. 2D Panel Behavior

Purpose

The 2D panel is where users draw and edit the Floor Plan. The drawing toolbar should follow the 2D panel so the relationship is obvious.

Recommended Behavior

  • When 2D and 3D are both visible, the 2D drawing tools should sit closer to the 2D panel than the 3D panel.
  • When 2D only is active, the 2D drawing tools should remain visible and centered within the 2D workspace.
  • When 3D only is active, 2D drawing tools should hide or become clearly unavailable.
  • The current active drawing tool should remain visually obvious.
  • The Shapes dropdown should show an active state when Rectangle, Circle, or Polygon is selected.
  • Undo and Redo should stay with the 2D drawing group because they affect drawing and editing changes.

User-Friendly Guidance

Use spatial placement to explain tool ownership. If a tool creates or edits 2D geometry, place it where the user is looking while editing 2D geometry.

Suggested 2D Tool Labels

  • Wall
  • Curve
  • Window
  • Area
  • Shapes
  • Point
  • Safety
  • Undo
  • Redo

11. 3D / Shared Viewer Behavior

Purpose

The 3D viewer needs camera and display controls, but it should not compete with the 2D drawing workflow.

Recommended Behavior

  • Keep Zoom In, Zoom Out, and Fit Plan in a shared viewer group.
  • Keep Reset 3D Camera in the shared viewer group, but make its 3D meaning clear.
  • If 3D only is active, prioritize the Reset 3D Camera control.
  • If 2D only is active, Reset 3D Camera can remain available but should be visually quieter or disabled if it does not apply.
  • Shared viewer controls should remain near the active workspace and should not be mistaken for drawing tools.

Suggested Viewer Labels

  • Zoom in
  • Zoom out
  • Fit plan
  • Reset 3D camera
  • View options

12. Panel Mode Behavior

Purpose

Panel mode should be understandable as a display choice, not two unrelated toggle buttons.

Recommended Display Modes

Use a single panel mode control with three options:

Option Meaning
2D only Show only the 2D floor plan editor.
3D only Show only the 3D viewer.
2D & 3D Show both panels side by side.

Recommended Behavior

  • Always keep at least one panel visible.
  • Make the active panel mode visually selected.
  • When switching to 2D only, center the 2D drawing tools in the available 2D workspace.
  • When switching to 3D only, hide or reduce 2D drawing tools and emphasize viewer controls.
  • When switching to 2D & 3D, keep the layout balanced and place 2D tools near the 2D side.

Suggested Copy

  • Panel
  • 2D only
  • 3D only
  • 2D & 3D

13. Visibility and Export Grouping

Object Visibility

Replace the generic Show Icons idea with clear object-specific visibility controls.

Recommended object visibility dropdown:

  • Show doors.
  • Show windows.
  • Show shapes.
  • Show points.
  • Show safety annotations.
  • Show room labels.

This makes the control easier to understand because users can choose exactly what appears in the workspace.

Floor Plan Image

The Floor Plan Image control should include:

  • A visibility toggle.
  • An opacity slider only when the image is visible and an image exists.

Do not show the opacity slider when it cannot affect anything.

Snap to Grid

Snap to Grid should stay near viewer or editing assist controls. It should feel like an editing aid, not an object type.

Export

Export should collect output actions in one place:

  • Export editable TXT.
  • Export GeoJSON.

The visible toolbar should show one Export entry at most, not separate export buttons.

14. User Flows

Flow A: Return to Dashboard

  1. User opens File.
  2. User selects Dashboard.
  3. If there are unsaved changes, the editor asks for confirmation.
  4. User confirms or cancels.
  5. User returns to /dashboard.

Flow B: Start a New File

  1. User opens File.
  2. User selects New File.
  3. If there are unsaved changes, the editor asks for confirmation.
  4. User confirms or cancels.
  5. User moves to /start.

Flow C: Draw in 2D

  1. User views the 2D panel.
  2. User sees drawing tools close to the 2D workspace.
  3. User selects Wall, Curve, Window, Area, Point, or Safety.
  4. The active tool state is visible.
  5. User can Undo or Redo from the same 2D tool group.

Flow C2: Choose a Shape Tool

  1. User views the 2D panel.
  2. User opens Shapes from the 2D drawing toolbar.
  3. User sees Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon grouped together.
  4. User selects one shape type.
  5. The Shapes control shows an active state while the selected shape tool is active.
  6. User still understands that shape behavior is part of the 2D editing workflow, not a 3D viewer control.

Flow D: Inspect in 3D

  1. User switches to 3D only or keeps 2D & 3D.
  2. User sees viewer controls separately from drawing tools.
  3. User uses Reset 3D Camera or zoom controls without scanning through drawing actions.

Flow E: Change Visible Objects

  1. User opens Object Visibility.
  2. User toggles doors, windows, shapes, points, safety annotations, or room labels.
  3. The workspace updates while keeping the dropdown state clear.

Flow F: Adjust Floor Plan Image

  1. User opens image visibility controls.
  2. User turns the Floor Plan Image on.
  3. The opacity slider appears.
  4. User adjusts opacity.
  5. If the image is turned off, the opacity slider is hidden.

Flow G: Switch Panel Mode

  1. User opens Panel control.
  2. User chooses 2D only, 3D only, or 2D & 3D.
  3. Panels update.
  4. Tool placement updates so controls still feel attached to the correct workspace.

15. Accessibility and Usability Notes

  • Icon-only buttons need clear accessible names and tooltips.
  • Controls should have at least a comfortable clickable area.
  • The active tool should be indicated by more than color alone.
  • Dropdown items should be keyboard reachable.
  • The Shapes dropdown should be keyboard reachable and should expose Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon as clear menu items.
  • Panel mode should announce the selected state.
  • Disabled controls should explain why they are unavailable where possible.
  • Toolbar groups should not overlap selection toolbars.
  • Long tool labels should collapse gracefully into icons with tooltips.
  • The layout should avoid horizontal overflow on smaller editor widths.
  • The UI should remain clear in light and dark editor themes.

16. Suggested UI Copy

File Menu

  • File
  • Dashboard
  • New File
  • Help

2D Drawing Tools

  • Wall
  • Curve
  • Window
  • Area
  • Shapes
  • Rectangle
  • Circle
  • Polygon
  • Point
  • Safety
  • Undo
  • Redo

Viewer Controls

  • Zoom in
  • Zoom out
  • Fit plan
  • Reset 3D camera
  • Snap to grid

Visibility

  • Object visibility
  • Show doors
  • Show windows
  • Show shapes
  • Show points
  • Show safety annotations
  • Show room labels

Floor Plan Image

  • Floor plan image
  • Show image
  • Image opacity

Panel Mode

  • Panel
  • 2D only
  • 3D only
  • 2D & 3D

Export

  • Export
  • Editable TXT
  • GeoJSON

17. Acceptance Criteria

File Dropdown

  • File dropdown shows Dashboard, New File, and Help.
  • Dashboard routes to /dashboard.
  • New File routes to /start.
  • Help routes to /help.
  • Disabled placeholder items are removed or avoided.
  • Leaving the editor through Dashboard or New File respects unsaved-change protection.

Toolbar Cleanup

  • Load Floorplan is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Save Editable TXT is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Export GeoJSON is not shown as a main toolbar button.
  • Load Floorplan is treated as part of Add Level.
  • Editable TXT and GeoJSON are grouped under Export.

Tool Grouping

  • 2D drawing tools are visually separate from viewer controls.
  • Wall, Curve, Window, Area, Shapes, Point, Safety Annotation, Undo, and Redo are grouped as 2D tools.
  • Shapes appears as one dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools.
  • Shapes contains Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  • Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon do not appear as separate top-level toolbar buttons.
  • Selecting a Shapes menu item makes the Shapes control visibly active.
  • Zoom, Fit Plan, Reset 3D Camera, visibility, Snap to Grid, Floor Plan Image, and panel controls are grouped as viewer or workspace controls.
  • The active drawing tool remains clear.

Panel Behavior

  • 2D only mode shows the 2D workspace and keeps 2D drawing tools available.
  • 3D only mode shows the 3D workspace and does not present 2D drawing tools as primary controls.
  • 2D & 3D mode shows both panels and keeps tool ownership visually clear.
  • Users cannot hide both panels at the same time.

Visibility

  • Object visibility uses clear object names.
  • Doors, windows, shapes, points, safety annotations, and room labels can be understood separately.
  • Generic Show Icons is replaced by specific visibility choices.
  • Floor Plan Image opacity appears only when it can be used.

Style

  • The editor keeps its current compact toolbar style.
  • Existing rounded controls, borders, shadows, and editor tokens are preserved.
  • The change does not introduce a marketing-style layout or unrelated visual system.

18. QA Scenarios

  1. User opens File and sees Dashboard, New File, and Help.
  2. User selects Dashboard with no unsaved changes and reaches the dashboard.
  3. User selects Dashboard with unsaved changes and sees a confirmation.
  4. User selects New File and reaches the start flow after any required confirmation.
  5. User can find Help from the File dropdown.
  6. User does not see disabled placeholder File menu items.
  7. User does not see Load Floorplan in the main toolbar.
  8. User can understand that floor plan loading belongs to Add Level.
  9. User does not see separate Save Editable TXT and Export GeoJSON toolbar buttons.
  10. User finds Editable TXT and GeoJSON under Export.
  11. User sees drawing tools grouped separately from viewer controls.
  12. User sees Shapes as a dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools.
  13. User opens Shapes and sees Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon.
  14. User selects Rectangle, Circle, or Polygon and sees Shapes become active.
  15. User does not see Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon as separate top-level toolbar buttons.
  16. User switches to 2D only and can still use drawing tools.
  17. User switches to 3D only and drawing tools are hidden or visually de-emphasized.
  18. User switches to 2D & 3D and can understand which tools belong to 2D.
  19. User toggles doors without also toggling all icons.
  20. User toggles windows without also toggling all icons.
  21. User toggles shapes separately from points and safety annotations.
  22. User toggles points and safety annotations separately.
  23. User toggles room labels separately.
  24. User turns on the Floor Plan Image and sees the opacity slider.
  25. User turns off the Floor Plan Image and the opacity slider no longer distracts.
  26. Keyboard-only user can reach File, drawing tools, Shapes, viewer controls, and panel mode.
  27. Toolbar groups do not overlap contextual selection toolbars.

19. Open Questions

Question Recommended default Owner
Should Help open /help in the same tab or a new tab? Same tab, with unsaved-change protection if leaving editor state. Product / Design
Should Add Level remain accessible from the File menu? Prefer no; keep File focused on navigation and help unless Product wants level management there. Product
Where should the Export entry live? Prefer the topbar near Save/Preview or a compact shared-control menu, not inside the 2D drawing tools. Design
Where should Shapes sit in the 2D tool order? Place it after Area and before Point so it reads as object geometry, not annotation. Design
Should 2D drawing tools hide completely in 3D only mode? Yes, hide them or clearly de-emphasize them so users do not try to draw in 3D. Product / Design
Should Reset 3D Camera be disabled in 2D only mode? Prefer disabled or visually quiet if the 3D panel is hidden. Design / Engineering
Should object visibility affect both 2D and 3D views or only the active panel? Prefer both views for consistency unless a panel-specific need is defined later. Product
Should Show shapes live in Object Visibility from v1? Yes, include it so shape visibility is managed with other object visibility controls. Product / Design

20. Risks

Risk Impact Mitigation
Toolbar becomes too fragmented. Users may need to look in too many places. Keep only three zones: File, 2D tools, shared viewer controls.
2D tools are hidden too aggressively. Users may think editing is unavailable. Hide 2D tools only in 3D only mode; show them clearly in 2D modes.
Export becomes hard to find. Users may miss downloadable outputs. Use a clear Export label and place it near top-level editor actions.
Visibility dropdown becomes too long. Users may avoid it. Keep only object-level visibility choices that users understand.
Shapes crowds the 2D toolbar. The toolbar may feel harder to scan. Use one Shapes dropdown instead of separate Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon buttons.
Shapes is mistaken for Area. Users may confuse room boundaries with room objects. Place Shapes near Area, but keep it as a clearly named dropdown with object-focused menu items.
The design drifts away from the current editor style. The editor feels inconsistent. Reuse current compact floating controls, icons, borders, shadows, and editor tokens.
Panel switching causes confusion. Users may lose track of tool ownership. Make panel mode explicit and move/de-emphasize tools based on visible panels.

21. Design Summary for UI UX Pro Max

The editor layout should remain visually conservative and workspace-focused. Keep the current MapThru editor shell, compact topbar, floating control surfaces, rounded icon buttons, soft borders, subtle shadows, and editor color tokens.

The main design improvement is clearer tool ownership:

  • File actions belong in the File dropdown.
  • 2D drawing tools belong with the 2D plan panel.
  • Shapes belongs as a dropdown inside the 2D drawing tools, with Rectangle, Circle, and Polygon grouped inside it.
  • Shared viewer controls belong in their own workspace control group.
  • Export actions belong under Export.
  • Visibility choices should name the actual objects users can show or hide, including shapes.
  • Panel mode should be one clear control with 2D only, 3D only, and 2D & 3D options.

This should make editor mode feel less crowded without changing the core editing workflow. The user should feel that the interface is guiding them: draw in 2D, inspect in 3D, control visibility from one place, and manage files from the top navigation.

issues.display_title: Issue #195: Update editor Pano with GoThru virtual tour picker
issues.main_description_html:
Source

  • Brainstorming file: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-07-editor-pano-gothru-dashboard-brainstorming.md
  • Branch/source docs: product-docs

RESULT

  • Branch: UI-UX-Update-editor-Pano-with-GoThru

Goal

Update the editor Information area Pano feature so users connect to the GoThru dashboard, choose a virtual tour, and then choose a pano image from that tour without leaving the editor.

User Experience

The Pano area must guide the user through this flow:

  1. Connect to the GoThru dashboard.
  2. Review connected account details.
  3. Select a virtual tour.
  4. Select a pano image from the chosen tour.
  5. Confirm or change the selected pano.

Required States

  • Not connected
  • Connecting
  • Connected
  • Connection expired
  • Connection failed
  • Loading virtual tours
  • No virtual tours
  • Virtual tours loaded
  • Virtual tour selected
  • Loading pano images
  • No pano images
  • Pano images loaded
  • Pano selected
  • Error loading tours
  • Error loading pano images

Requirements

  • If the user is not connected, show a Connect button in the Pano area.
  • Clicking Connect opens a same-page GoThru dashboard login dialog.
  • The login dialog includes email address, password, Google login, and cancel.
  • If connected, show avatar, full name, email, connection status, and Change Account.
  • Connection status must support Connected, Expired, and Failed.
  • Change Account uses the same connection/login flow as Connect.
  • After connection, show a virtual tour list.
  • Each virtual tour row shows virtual tour name, tour key, and total image count.
  • After selecting a tour, show a pano image list.
  • Each pano image row shows a 1:1 thumbnail, sequence image number, and pano name.
  • Selected pano should be clearly visible and easy to change.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Users can connect to GoThru from the editor Information Pano area.
  • Users can change the connected GoThru account without leaving the editor.
  • Connected account data is visible and readable.
  • Expired and failed connection states provide clear recovery actions.
  • Users can browse virtual tours and select one.
  • Users can browse pano images and select one.
  • Empty, loading, and error states are designed for tours and pano images.
  • The experience fits within the editor Information area without feeling crowded.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign the whole editor.
  • Do not redesign all Information tabs.
  • Do not replace the current MapThru login session.
  • Do not force the user to leave the editor page.
  • Do not add billing, publishing, or project management actions to the Pano area.

issues.display_title: Issue #196: Create GoThru connection login modal
issues.main_description_html:
Source

  • Brainstorming file: docs/superpowers/brainstorming/2026-07-07-gothru-connection-login-modal-brainstorming.md
  • Branch/source docs: product-docs

RESULT

  • Branch: UI-UX-Create-GoThru-connection-login

Goal

Create a same-page GoThru account connection login modal for the profile GoThru dashboard connection card.

User Experience

The profile page keeps the GoThru dashboard connection card as the entry point. When the user clicks Connect GoThru dashboard or Change account, a dialog opens on the same page.

The dialog allows the user to connect a GoThru dashboard account using email/password or Google login. After a successful connection, the dialog closes, the connection card updates, and the user sees a success notification.

Requirements

  • Keep the GoThru connection action inside the profile page connection card.
  • Open a modal/dialog when the user clicks Connect GoThru dashboard.
  • Open the same modal/dialog when the user clicks Change account.
  • The modal includes:
    • Email address field
    • Password field
    • Connect account primary button
    • Continue with Google button
    • Cancel/close action
  • Canceling the modal must not change the current account connection.
  • Failed login keeps the modal open and shows a clear error.
  • Successful login closes the modal automatically.
  • The profile connection card updates after successful connection.
  • Show a success notification after connection or account change.

Suggested Copy

  • Dialog title: Connect GoThru account
  • Dialog helper: Sign in to the GoThru dashboard account you want to link to this workspace.
  • Primary button: Connect account
  • Google button: Continue with Google
  • Success notification: GoThru account connected successfully.
  • Change-account success notification: GoThru account changed successfully.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Users can start GoThru connection from the profile page.
  • Connect GoThru dashboard opens the login dialog on the same page.
  • Change account opens the login dialog on the same page.
  • The dialog includes email address, password, and Google login.
  • Canceling the dialog does not change the current connection.
  • Failed login keeps the dialog open and shows a clear error.
  • Successful login closes the dialog.
  • The profile card updates after successful connection.
  • The user receives a clear success notification.
  • The flow works well on desktop and mobile.

Non-Goals

  • Do not redesign the full profile page.
  • Do not redesign the main MapThru login page.
  • Do not sign the user out of MapThru when connecting GoThru.
  • Do not replace the current MapThru dashboard session.
  • Do not combine disconnect confirmation with the login dialog.
